cards.title: Use voluntary written product goals in post-purchase onboarding
cards.summary: A self-chosen written commitment can make a product-use intention easier to revisit.
cards.use_when: Customers buy a product that requires a routine or learning period.
steps: Invite the customer to choose a realistic product-use goal in their own words.
Offer an optional saved reminder and useful setup instructions.
Measure actual use, satisfaction and repeat purchase against a simpler onboarding flow.
caveats: Ecommerce adaptation of commitment research; do not assume a purchase lift or make participation compulsory.

cards.title: Record independent judgments before debating ecommerce decisions
cards.summary: Publicly defending an initial position can make it harder to update when new evidence appears.
cards.use_when: A team is selecting products, creative concepts or experiment winners.
steps: Have reviewers record initial judgments privately before discussion.
Compare evidence and assumptions, then invite revisions.
Document what new customer or performance evidence would change the decision.
caveats: The source describes judgment experiments, not a measured ecommerce effect.

cards.title: Treat praise-contest submissions as selected marketing material
cards.summary: A contest asking people to praise a product selects and encourages favorable accounts; it is not an unbiased satisfaction survey.
cards.use_when: A brand collects customer essays or promotional testimonials.
steps: Collect honest feedback separately from promotional contests.
Record incentives and obtain permission before reusing submissions.
Compare recurring claims with independent customer feedback and product evidence.
caveats: Do not present incentivized praise as representative customer sentiment or require positive marketplace reviews.

cards.title: Separate effort invested from the value of a commerce project
cards.summary: Effort justification can cause teams to overvalue something because it was difficult to create.
cards.use_when: A costly launch, loyalty program or site redesign is under review.
steps: List customer outcomes and forward-looking costs independently of work already spent.
Compare continuation with a simpler alternative using the same metrics.
Stop or change the project when evidence no longer supports its value.
caveats: An adaptation of effort-justification research; adding customer friction is not a retention strategy.

cards.title: Distinguish reward-driven purchases from durable product preference
cards.summary: Behavior maintained by a strong external reward may not persist when that reward ends.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a discounted trial or loyalty incentive.
steps: State the incentive and its duration before customers join.
Measure repeat purchases and product satisfaction after the disclosed reward period.
Compare with a suitable baseline before attributing retention to brand preference.
caveats: Honor promised rewards; historical psychology findings do not establish ecommerce retention rates.

cards.title: Audit checkout for lowball pricing after customer commitment
cards.summary: Customers may rationalize staying after an attractive initial deal worsens; conversion alone does not justify hidden fees.
cards.use_when: Reviewing advertised offers and checkout totals.
steps: Compare the ad and product-page promise with the final price and required charges.
Disclose material terms before customers invest time in checkout.
Fix mismatches and track abandonment, complaints and refunds alongside conversion.
caveats: The source describes deceptive car-dealer lowballing; this card adapts it as an ecommerce diagnostic, not a tactic to copy.

cards.title: Keep public product-use commitments optional
cards.summary: Public commitments can support follow-through while also making people reluctant to change their minds.
cards.use_when: Designing a customer challenge or community program.
steps: Offer a private participation option alongside public sharing.
Let customers select achievable goals and revise them.
Measure completion and satisfaction without shaming dropouts or obstructing cancellations.
caveats: Public commitment is not consent for unrelated marketing and does not prove product effectiveness.

generation_method: Local source-grounded extraction after provider failures; prior reservations retained
